newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes up on technical adjustment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes up on technical adjustment.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher on technical adjustment and an early rebound in Tokyo but the market was still void of buyers, dealers said.
"I think it's more of an adjustment than anything else," said a dealer. "The better Japanese prices in the first two sessions are also a factor."

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for November RSS1 buyer at 309.50 cents ($1.23) a kg, up one cent from Friday. November SMR 20 was also a cent higher at 308.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 305 cents, SMR 10 at 306, SMR 5 at 317, SMR L at 342, SMR CV at 362 and drum latex at 234.
The Malaysian rubber market has been depressed for most of this month, with notable absence by Chinese, European and Middle East buyers who did active short-covering until August.
A fresh round of buying could, however, see the RSS1 and SMR 20 rising by at least "three and five cents", said a dealer.
The INRO five-day moving average was 239.13 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 25 from 239.03 on Oct 24. The daily indicator price was 239.50 against 239.28.
